base_member_text: [L26-L47,L278-L285] (MED/unsafe unload loop) Finalization repeatedly calls dlclose on one saved handle until a shell-based lsof probe says the path is absent, which can reuse an already-closed handle or unload a library still shared by another wrapper instance.

[L43-L47] (MED/nonportable shell probe) isloaded depends on external lsof and interpolates an unquoted absolute path into a shell pipeline, so spaces or shell metacharacters break the check and supported non-Unix platforms cannot use it.

[L26-L38] (LOW/platform/bytes handling) dlclose assumes a loadable libdl plus an unversioned suffix and compares dlerror's bytes result to a str literal, so its error classification is unreliable on Python 3 and several declared platforms.
audit_member_text: [L26-L38,L278-L285] (MED/portability/resource-lifecycle) The explicit unload path assumes a Unix-style libdl and repeatedly calls dlclose based on an external lsof/grep probe, which is not a reliable or portable library-lifetime contract (notably on Windows and systems without lsof).

[L45-L47] (MED/command-construction) isloaded interpolates an unquoted absolute library path into a shell command, so spaces or shell metacharacters in a legitimate path can make the load check incorrect.
